title: Lists
summary: Store collections of items and process them.

exercises.title: Second Item
exercises.prompt: For `fruits = ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]` print the second item, then the length of the list on the next line.

exercises.title: Append
exercises.prompt: Start with `nums = [1, 2, 3]`, append `4`, and print the list.

exercises.title: Remove
exercises.prompt: Start with `letters = ["a", "b", "c"]`, remove `"b"`, and print the list.

exercises.title: Sum with a Loop
exercises.prompt: For `nums = [4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42]` use a for loop to print the sum.
exercises.solution:
nums = [4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42]
total = 0
for n in nums:
    total += n
print(total)

exercises.title: First Three
exercises.prompt: For `nums = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]` print the first three items as a list.

exercises.title: Backwards
exercises.prompt: For `items = ["x", "y", "z"]` print each item on its own line in reverse order.

exercises.title: Squares
exercises.prompt: Use a list comprehension to print the squares of 1 to 5 as a list.
exercises.solution: print([n * n for n in range(1, 6)])

exercises.title: Filter Evens
exercises.prompt: Use a list comprehension to print the even numbers from 1 to 10 as a list.
hints: Add if n % 2 == 0 at the end.
exercises.solution: print([n for n in range(1, 11) if n % 2 == 0])

exercises.title: Max and Min
exercises.prompt: Read one line of space-separated integers. Print the largest and smallest separated by a space.
hints: input().split() gives a list of strings.
exercises.solution:
nums = [int(x) for x in input().split()]
print(max(nums), min(nums))
